key_insight: In a multi-step coding setting, the researchers identified a small set of attention heads whose outputs encode the model’s next sub-goal. This suggests that some internal representations track what the model is working toward, rather than only its immediate output.
problem_solved: How can researchers identify internal goal representations in LLMs and distinguish them from the specific steps used to complete a task?
method: Construct a coding environment with multiple sub-tasks to evaluate goal-seeking behavior and sub-goal selection.
Analyze attention-head outputs to locate representations of the next sub-goal.
Identify a sparse set of attention heads that carries this sub-goal information.
impact: Identifying sub-goal representations could help practitioners interpret how LLMs organize multi-step work and develop tools for monitoring goal-directed behavior. The supplied abstract is truncated, so broader predictive or control capabilities cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: A branching task diagram showing one goal reached through multiple execution paths.
A coding workflow highlighting the current task and next sub-goal.
An attention-head grid with the small set of goal-encoding heads highlighted.
A model cutaway linking attention-head outputs to a decoded sub-goal label.
paper_authors: Arnab Sen Sharma, Eric Todd, Sheridan Feucht, Andy Arditi, Rohit Gandikota
